subject: Logic
title: When You're the Fallacy User
description: A micro-lesson that makes When You're the Fallacy User usable.

hook.text: You've been spotting fallacies in others. But the hardest ones to catch are your own.

buildup.text: We all use fallacies—usually unintentionally. Bias and habit make us reach for shortcuts.

discovery.text: Catching yourself requires a pause: "Why do I believe this? What's my actual evidence?"

twist.text: The more confident you feel, the more you should check. Certainty is often where fallacies hide best.

climax.text: Self-correction is the highest form of logical thinking. It's harder and rarer than correcting others.

quiz.question: When are your own fallacies hardest to catch?
